english.title: Vote as proxy in parliamentary or local government election for more than two persons who are not relatives
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of an illegal practice in that you voted in

(A)_[a constituency, namely **(..SPECIFY CONSTITUENCY..) at a parliamentary]_
(B)_[an electoral area, namely **(..SPECIFY AREA..), at a local government]_

election as proxy for more than two persons, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSONS..) of whom you were not the spouse, civil partner, parent, grandparent, brother, sister, child or grandchild
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 61(4) and (7) and 169 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
votes at a parliamentary election in a constituency or at a local government election in an electoral area
as proxy for more than two persons of whom he is not the spouse, civil partner, parent, grandparent, brother, sister, child or grandchild

english.notes:
61(7) An offence under this section shall be an illegal practice but -
(a) the court before whom a person is convicted of any such offence may, if they think it just in the special circumstances of the case, mitigate or entirely remit any incapacity imposed by virtue of section 173; and (b) a candidate shall not be liable, nor shall his election be avoided, for an illegal practice under this section of any agent of his other than an offence under subsection (5) above.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 176

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
